verdict.text:
Track 1 is not measurable on this run. Every slot has `support_gold_missing = 0`, and the `gold_slots` for all thirty requirements are empty strings — the adjudicated labels simply have not been produced. The 0.0 precision/recall/f1 across scope, condition, actor, modalVerb and action is therefore an artifact of absent gold, not evidence that CoT failed at missing-slot detection. The same applies to the implied-slot fill_rate (n_implied = 0) and to the 0.833 "agreement rate", which arises only because empty gold defaults to "complete" while the LLM flagged something missing in five items. Nothing about fabrication risk can be concluded from these numbers either way.

That said, the raw human conversions in the worst-example dump *do* carry `<MISSING_*>` markers, so the information exists and only needs adjudicating or parsing into the gold fields. That is the single highest-value next step; until it is done this run contributes nothing to the experiment's central question.

On Track 2, the LLM sits below the human ceiling but not catastrophically: 0.438 vs 0.576 on seq_ratio, 0.296 vs 0.473 on Jaccard. With standard deviations of 0.24–0.31 and 89 non-independent pairs from 30 items, that gap is roughly half a standard deviation and is driven by a small tail rather than a uniform deficit. The tail is diagnostic. 83-Signal (0.009), 1504-Signal (0.022) and 2943-Signal (0.033) are all inputs with no usable description; humans wrapped their output in the Rimay boilerplate ("For all users, `<MISSING_CONDITION>` the App must …") while the LLM emitted a bare placeholder fragment with no scope prefix and no condition marker. This is template non-compliance, not semantic
